late: Assessment and late submission policy. Students should upload coursework through the learning portal before the stated deadline and retain the submission receipt. Late submissions are normally penalized according to the course handbook. An extension may be considered when a student has a documented circumstance and submits the required request through the course office. Illness extensions require medical evidence before the deadline. This requirement is an exception to the normal late-submission rule; a request submitted after the deadline may be reviewed, but approval is not guaranteed. Students should not assume that a message to a teaching assistant automatically changes the deadline. The final submitted file should be readable and follow the file format stated in the assignment instructions. If the portal shows an error, take a screenshot and contact the course office promptly. A receipt is useful evidence that the upload completed, but it does not itself approve an extension. Course-specific instructions may add requirements, so students should check the latest assignment page as well as this general policy. Keep copies of drafts and submitted files until grades are finalized. When the learning portal becomes unavailable shortly before a deadline, students should record the time, preserve any visible error message, avoid repeatedly submitting duplicate files without checking the receipt, and contact the course office using the published support route so that staff can review the evidence and explain the next steps without assuming that an extension has automatically been approved.
password: Account access and password recovery. If you forget your password, use the password recovery link on the official sign-in page and follow the instructions sent to your registered email address. Reset a forgotten password using the recovery link. Never share recovery codes with another person, including someone claiming to be support staff. A support worker should not ask you to disclose a one-time code or your full password. If you no longer have access to the registered email, contact the IT help desk and be ready to verify your account through the approved process. Do not repeatedly submit passwords on a page whose address you cannot verify. Sign out of shared computers when finished, and use a unique password for each important account. Password resets may take several minutes to propagate across connected services. If a reset email does not arrive, check the spam folder and confirm that the registered address is correct before requesting another email. The IT help desk can investigate locked accounts, but it cannot bypass the identity-verification policy. Keep recovery information private and up to date.
assignment: Coursework submission instructions. Upload assignments through the learning portal. Students should open the correct course page, choose the relevant assignment, attach the final file, and wait for the confirmation screen. Submit the final file as a PDF unless the assignment instructions explicitly request another format. A saved draft is not the same as a completed submission, and students should verify the submission receipt after uploading. If the portal rejects a file, check the file size and format before contacting support. Do not email a copy as a substitute unless the instructor has explicitly authorized email submission. The portal timestamp is used to establish when a submission was received. Students are responsible for checking that the uploaded file opens and contains the intended work. A late upload is normally subject to the late-submission policy. If the portal is unavailable near a deadline, keep evidence of the problem and contact the course office as soon as possible. Assignment pages may contain task-specific rules, and those rules take precedence over this general guide where they clearly differ. Never upload another student's work as your own.
contractor: Remote work and contractor eligibility. Contractors can work remotely only if the signed contract permits it. The contract should be checked for location, data-handling, equipment, and availability requirements before remote work begins. Employee rules do not automatically apply to contractors, because the terms may be different. A manager's informal verbal approval is not a replacement for a contract clause or a formally approved amendment. Contractors handling confidential material must use approved systems and follow the organization's security requirements regardless of work location. Some projects require on-site attendance for particular activities, even where other work may be completed remotely. The project lead should clarify any uncertainty with procurement or the contract owner before work is performed. A contractor should not infer permission from the fact that another contractor works from home. Written authorization and the signed agreement are the primary evidence for this decision. If a contract is silent about remote work, ask the contract owner for clarification rather than assuming that remote work is allowed. These conditions protect both the organization and the contractor by making expectations explicit.
printer: Printer troubleshooting guide. For blank printer pages, check ink levels and run the cleaning utility. After cleaning, print a test page and inspect whether the output has improved. Confirm that the printer is selected in the application and that the correct paper size is configured. If the printer reports a paper jam, follow the manufacturer's safe jam-removal instructions and do not pull forcefully on stuck paper. Check that the cartridge or toner is seated correctly and that protective seals have been removed from a new cartridge. A printer may need a short pause after a cleaning cycle before another test is attempted. If only one application prints blank pages, try a test from a different application to isolate the problem. Restarting the printer can resolve temporary communication errors, but repeated restarts will not fix an empty cartridge or blocked printhead. If the issue continues, record the printer model and any displayed error message before contacting support. Shared printers may be subject to local maintenance schedules, so do not disassemble equipment unless you are authorized to do so. Replace consumables using the approved supplies for that model.
remote_notice: Project remote-work notice. This notice is a general project communication about work location and scheduling. It states that all project contributors may work remotely for up to two days each week when their tasks can be completed online. The notice asks contributors to coordinate meeting times, protect confidential files, and remain reachable during agreed working hours. It also says that team leads may adjust schedules for project needs and that on-site sessions should be announced in advance. However, the contractor policy states that contractors can work remotely only if the signed contract permits it. These statements may conflict for a contractor whose signed contract does not authorize remote work. The general project notice should not be treated as proof that a contract has been amended. Before acting on the general notice, the contractor should ask the contract owner or procurement team to resolve the conflict in writing. The organization should clarify which rule has priority, record any approved change, and communicate the same decision to the project lead and contractor. Contributors should not infer permission solely because a colleague follows a different schedule. The notice is provided for the synthetic retrieval exercise and is not an actual organizational policy.
